items.title: I Pulled a Drive From My NAS — Watch ZFS Fix Itself
items.description: In this video I build a RAIDZ1 pool with a hot spare in TrueNAS Community Edition, then physically pull a drive to trigger a real failure. items.title: State Of Self-Hosting Week 37 — GitHub Outages, the Memory Tax & HA Proxy Manager
items.description: In this week's State of Self-Hosting livestream we recapped the Selfh.st newsletters for Week 37 — covering the GitHub outage problem and why I'm migrating repos to Forgejo, the Backblaze drive reliability report, and the brutal hard drive and DDR memory price spike hitting homelab builders. We also dug into HA Proxy Manager for high availability, compared RackNerd vs Hetzner VPS pricing live, talked NetBird BYOP reverse proxying, and answered community questions on self-hosted mail servers, Seagate vs WD drive failure rates, and AI watermarking. Plus new self-hosted finance and fitness apps like Sure, Securo, and Open Gym. --- 📋 What We Covered: • GitHub Dependency & Forgejo — Why repeated GitHub outages and OAuth dependency pushed me to mirror and migrate projects to self-hosted Forgejo. • Disappearing Blogs & Unsearchable Discord — How knowledge is vanishing into Discord tickets and short-form video, and the bot that summarizes closed support tickets to keep answers searchable. • New Self-Hosted Finance & Fitness Apps — Sure, Securo, Open Gym and Hammer — finance and gym apps are in a golden era of self-hosted development right now. • The Memory and Hard Drive Price Crisis — 16GB of DDR5 now costs as much as a whole 4-bay NAS, and used drives have jumped from $10 to $25+ per terabyte. • Backblaze Drive Reliability Report — A peer-reviewed study of 443,000 drives points to Western Digital and HGST/Hitachi as the most reliable picks, with live shopping on Server Part Deals. • High Availability with HA Proxy Manager — Plans to run the wiki on both a VPS and TrueNAS with round-robin and failover so security reboots stop causing 404s. • RackNerd vs Hetzner VPS Pricing — A live price comparison showing why a $22/year RackNerd box still wins for running Uptime Kuma and Gotify outside the house. • Why I Don't Recommend Self-Hosting Email — Blocked SMTP ports, spam filter reputation, and mail servers being the second-biggest attack target after WordPress. • AI Watermarking & the Debian Vote — Debian voting to allow AI contributions, LibreOffice going the other way, and why watermarking may falsely credit AI for human writing. --- 🔗 Important Links: Self-Hosted Newsletter ➤ https://selfh.st Stop Trusting GitHub With Your Projects — Self-Host Forgejo ➤ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_kpayAlRZA items.title: Cal.com Went Closed Source — So I Switched to This
items.description: Cal.com went closed source in April 2026, so I went looking for a replacement. items.title: Keep Your Drives Alive Longer: TrueNAS Drive Health Guide
items.description: Hard drive prices have surged nearly 50% thanks to the AI storage crunch, so keeping your existing drives healthy matters more than ever. In this video I show you how to set up automatic SMART testing on TrueNAS after iX removed it from the GUI, how to actually read a SMART report and the 5 metrics that predict failure, plus ZFS scrubs and the other tasks that extend drive life. We cover cron jobs, the Scrutiny app, and how SMART and ZFS work together. --- 🔗 Important Links: 📖 Blog Post: Getting SMART About Your Data ➤ https://blog.serversatho.me/getting-smart-about-your-data-why-drive-health-isnt-enough/ TrueNAS Drive Health Management Docs ➤ https://www.truenas.com/docs/ Scrutiny GitHub ➤ https://github.com/AnalogJ/scrutiny Backblaze Drive Stats ➤ https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/resources/hard-drive-test-data *COMMANDS USED IN THIS VIDEO* (Replace /dev/sda with your own drive. Find yours with the first command.) # List every drive and its type (sata/sas = scsi, nvme = nvme) smartctl --scan # Run a SMART test on one drive by hand smartctl -t short /dev/sda smartctl -t long /dev/sda smartctl -t short /dev/nvme0 # Test EVERY drive at once, the TrueNAS way (returns null on success) midclt call disk.smart_test SHORT '["*"]' midclt call disk.smart_test LONG '["*"]' # Portable alternative that works on any Linux box for dev in $(smartctl --scan | cut -d' ' -f1); do smartctl -t short "$dev"; done # Read the results smartctl -H /dev/sda # quick pass/fail summary smartctl -A /dev/sda # per-attribute table (the 5 metrics live here) smartctl -l selftest /dev/sda # history of tests you have run smartctl -a /dev/sda # everything at once # Abort a running test smartctl -X /dev/sda # Cross-check pool health against SMART zpool status --- 📌 Timestamps: 0:00 Intro 0:47 SMART Drama 1:36 Running SMART test from CLI 3:21 Turning SMART into a cronjob 5:08 Using Scrutiny instead 6:44 How to read a SMART test 9:27 Setting up ZFS scrub tasks 11:04 When to replace a drive 12:12 SMART + ZFS for the win 12:51 Conclusion --- 🔗 Helpful Links & Community 🛠️ Hire me for your project: ➤ https://links.serversatho.me/hire 💬 Join the discussion on Discord: ➤ https://links.serversatho.me/discord 📖 Check out the Wiki for setup guides & tips: ➤ https://wiki.serversatho.me/ 🎉 Support the channel on Patreon: ➤ https://links.serversatho.me/patreon Join this channel to get access to support me: ➤ https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCx0ObGO7YJZpPPf6tbHpqPQ/join 👉 Follow me everywhere ➤ https://serversatho.me ☕ Want to say thank you? In this video I show you how to set up automatic SMART testing on TrueNAS after iX removed it from the GUI, how to actually read a SMART report and the 5 metrics that predict failure, plus ZFS scrubs and the other tasks that extend drive life. We cover cron jobs, the Scrutiny app, and how SMART and ZFS work together. --- 🔗 Important Links: 📖 Blog Post: Getting SMART About Your Data ➤ https://blog.serversatho.me/getting-smart-about-your-data-why-drive-health-isnt-enough/ TrueNAS Drive Health Management Docs ➤ https://www.truenas.com/docs/ Scrutiny GitHub ➤ https://github.com/AnalogJ/scrutiny Backblaze Drive Stats ➤ https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/resources/hard-drive-test-data *COMMANDS USED IN THIS VIDEO* (Replace /dev/sda with your own drive. Find yours with the first command.) # List every drive and its type (sata/sas = scsi, nvme = nvme) smartctl --scan # Run a SMART test on one drive by hand smartctl -t short /dev/sda smartctl -t long /dev/sda smartctl -t short /dev/nvme0 # Test EVERY drive at once, the TrueNAS way (returns null on success) midclt call disk.smart_test SHORT '["*"]' midclt call disk.smart_test LONG '["*"]' # Portable alternative that works on any Linux box for dev in $(smartctl --scan | cut -d' ' -f1); do smartctl -t short "$dev"; done # Read the results smartctl -H /dev/sda # quick pass/fail summary smartctl -A /dev/sda # per-attribute table (the 5 metrics live here) smartctl -l selftest /dev/sda # history of tests you have run smartctl -a /dev/sda # everything at once # Abort a running test smartctl -X /dev/sda # Cross-check pool health against SMART zpool status --- 📌 Timestamps: 0:00 Intro 0:47 SMART Drama 1:36 Running SMART test from CLI 3:21 Turning SMART into a cronjob 5:08 Using Scrutiny instead 6:44 How to read a SMART test 9:27 Setting up ZFS scrub tasks 11:04 When to replace a drive 12:12 SMART + ZFS for the win 12:51 Conclusion --- 🔗 Helpful Links & Community 🛠️ Hire me for your project: ➤ https://links.serversatho.me/hire 💬 Join the discussion on Discord: ➤ https://links.serversatho.me/discord 📖 Check out the Wiki for setup guides & tips: ➤ https://wiki.serversatho.me/ 🎉 Support the channel on Patreon: ➤ https://links.serversatho.me/patreon Join this channel to get access to support me: ➤ https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCx0ObGO7YJZpPPf6tbHpqPQ/join 👉 Follow me everywhere ➤ https://serversatho.me ☕ Want to say thank you? items.title: Euro-Office: Europe's Microsoft 365 Killer, Deployed & Diffed [2026]
items.description: Euro Office launched as Europe's open-source answer to Microsoft 365 — so I deployed the Document Server on TrueNAS with Docker, wired it into Nextcloud as the new "Nextcloud Office" backend, and demoed the real-time collaborative editors. Then I diffed all four core repositories against OnlyOffice to find out what actually changed.
